question:
A 60-year-old man with an 8-year history of type 2 diabetes is brought to the emergency department
following a hypoglycemic episode at home, during which he experienced tremors, sweating, and
confusion. His fingerstick glucose level is 44 mg/dL (reference range, 70–100). The patient manages
his diabetes with glyburide 10 mg daily and controls his hypertension with labetalol 200 mg twice daily.
Three months ago, he underwent unilateral nephrectomy for localized renal-cell carcinoma. His most
recent estimated glomerular filtration rate was 55 mL/min/1.73 m² (reference range, ≥60). Which of the
following mechanisms most likely contributed to this patient’s hypoglycemia? Answer Choices: (A)
Reduced hepatic glucose output (B) Impaired gluconeogenesis (C) Enhanced peripheral glucose
uptake (D) Increased glucagon-like peptide-1 levels (E) Enhanced insulin sensitivity due to
beta-blockade (F) Impaired adrenergic response (G) Decreased sulfonylurea clearance (H) Decreased
cortisol response (I) Increased insulin secretion from beta cells (J) Impaired glycogen storage
 A. Increased insulin secretion from beta cells
B. Impaired gluconeogenesis
C. Enhanced insulin sensitivity due to beta-blockade
D. Enhanced peripheral glucose uptake
E. Decreased sulfonylurea clearance
F. Increased glucagon-like peptide-1 levels
G. Decreased cortisol response
H. Impaired adrenergic response
I. Reduced hepatic glucose output
J. Impaired glycogen storage
